transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-11
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Nora Voss (Redwood SE), Carlos Romero (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Cedarview), Samir Das (Cedarview), Alicia Gomez (Cedarview), Tom Reynolds (Cedarview)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff for Cedarview Health to align on scope (hosted vs private), security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), pilot timeline, and next steps. Agreed to run a short pilot on Dedicated capacity with an optional Private/VPC deep dive. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Maya: ok, uh hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and this is Liam our CSM and Nora and Carlos from engineering, we'll keep it pretty focused, want to make sure we understand your goals and any blockers for the onboarding pilot

[00:18] Dr. Elena: thanks Maya, yeah we, we're excited, Cedarview is looking to roll out clinical note summarization and triage suggestions in Q2, want to make sure latency and PHI policies are covered, and we need to understand Dedicated vs private options

[00:36] Liam: great, can you, Samir or Elena, give us a quick overview of current infra and what success looks like? like qps, latency targets, expected monthly token volume?

[00:50] Samir: sure, today we process about 500 reqs per min during peak, average payloads are 1.5k tokens, our SLA is 300ms P95 for short prompts but for the summarization flow we can tolerate up to 800ms but want consistent tail latency, monthly tokens maybe 120M-150M depending on pilot scope

[01:12] Nora: ok that's helpful; with Redwood Dedicated we can allocate GPU pools sized to meet predictable throughput; we also have autoscaling and burst capacity if needed, re: latency tail we use continuous batching + prefix KV cache to reduce per-token compute and improve P95

[01:34] Alicia: question on data handling: we are regulated, need SOC 2 type 2, audit logs, and KMS/HSM for key management, also SSO with SAML and RBAC, can you confirm those are supported?

[01:50] Carlos: yes absolutely, Redwood Private supports VPC-deployed control plane and can integrate with customer KMS, we have audit logs and session-level traces in Redwood Console. For hosted API we have SOC2 attestation and contractual DPA, for Private we can provide additional attestation and on-prem options

[02:12] Tom: and how about data residency? our legal team wants logs to stay in our VPC and not be pulled into a multi-tenant control plane

[02:24] Liam: for Dedicated we still manage control plane but data plane can be isolated; for Private deployment the customer controls the control plane and data never leaves your VPC unless you opt in; we'll share a diagram in the follow-up

[02:40] Dr. Elena: great, and pricing question — Dedicated costs vs hosted? our procurement will need a rough number for budgeting

[02:52] Maya: we'll send a pricing sheet, but rough guidance: hosted is usage-based (per-token), Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; depends on size of GPU pool and autoscaling, we can ballpark based on your expected QPS and token volumes, we'll attach an example SOW and T-shirt sizing in the follow-up

[03:14] Samir: technical question — we're planning to use an open model, maybe a 13b quantized var, do you support custom model uploads or only curated catalog? and what's the quantization story?

[03:30] Nora: we onboard both verified open models and customer models for Private/Dedicated. For quantization we support 8-bit and experimental 4-bit profiles depending on workload. Our runtime does kernel selection and compilation for the chosen profile, and we provide recommended quant profiles per workload to balance quality vs cost

[03:50] Carlos: quick note, sometimes transcriptions show K V cache or KV chache in docs, yeah we mean KV cache, and we'll include the recommended caching config for your prompt pattern

[04:05] Alicia: on encryption, where are keys stored? we have enterprise KMS and need HSM-backed keys for some flows

[04:13] Carlos: we integrate with customer KMS via standard APIs, can support HSM-backed KMS, plus envelope encryption for tokens at rest; we'll include the security doc with supported integrations

[04:30] Dr. Elena: onboarding timeline — we want to go live with a pilot by mid-Feb; is that realistic?

[04:40] Maya: yes that's doable; typical flow: sign SOW / PO, provision Dedicated or Private POC, run a 2-4 week pilot with Redwood SEs helping with perf benchmarks, then iterate and roll out, timeline depends on procurement speed and your infra handoffs

[04:56] Samir: about benchmarks — can we run a perf test with our sample payloads? we need P95 numbers across a couple of peak scenarios

[05:08] Nora: absolutely, please send a representative workload and keys (sanitized) or sample logs; we'll run Benchmarks on a Dedicated pool with your model + quant profile and share a spreadsheet with latency/cost breakdown and token-level analytics in Console

[05:24] Tom: security checklist — can you support SSO with SCIM provisioning? our HR/IT want auto provisioning for SSO groups

[05:34] Carlos: yes SCIM + SAML is supported, RBAC groups syncable; we'll provide the SSO quickstart doc and a checklist for IT integration

[05:48] Dr. Elena: any gotchas with on-prem or air-gapped options? we might have a future need for air-gapped so curious now

[05:56] Carlos: air-gapped is a heavier lift, needs a private package install and we typically coordinate with infra and ops teams; for initial pilot Dedicated in your cloud region is faster, then consider private or on-prem for later phases

[06:12] Alicia: legal will ask about data retention and logs, can you set retention policies per environment?

[06:20] Liam: yes retention configurable; for Private you control retention policies; for Dedicated and hosted we have configurable retention windows and exportable audit logs for compliance

[06:34] Nora: also note model rollouts: we support pinned versions and can do canary or A/B rollouts with automatic fallback if quality regressions are detected, which might help for clinical use cases

[06:52] Samir: ok good; question on SDKs — we saw examples in docs but our app is mostly python-based, any quickstarts?

[07:00] Maya: yes Python and Node SDKs, plus curl examples; we'll share a quickstart repo link in follow-up

[07:12] Tom: monitoring — is there token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards? we want granular chargeback for teams

[07:22] Liam: that's in Redwood Console; per-route, per-token costing, latency breakdown, traces; we can enable longer retention for observability as an add-on

[07:36] Dr. Elena: for pilot success criteria: 1) P95 latency under 800ms for summarization, 2) cost per call under $0.10 for the current model profile, 3) no PHI leakage per security review, and 4) end-to-end SSO/RBAC working — does that sound reasonable?

[07:58] Maya: yes that's a good start; we'll capture those as acceptance criteria for the pilot and align on metrics to track in Console

[08:12] Samir: do you support automatic batching for small prompts? some of our flows are chatty and would benefit from batching but we need consistent latency buckets

[08:24] Nora: yes we have workload-aware batching with latency SLOs; you can tune batch windows or prioritize low-latency routes to reduce batch size; we also do smart routing across model variants for cost savings

[08:40] Alicia: procurement will want to see SOC2 report and a sample DPA, can you send that?

[08:48] Liam: yes will attach, and for Private deployment we can discuss additional contractual terms

[09:00] Dr. Elena: any required firewall rules or IP whitelists for Dedicated?

[09:08] Carlos: we'll provide a network checklist; Dedicated requires certain egress/ingress ports and IP ranges; for Private we do VPC peering or private link options depending on cloud

[09:20] Samir: regarding model hosting — if we bring our own model, do you help with conversion and quantization or do we manage that?

[09:30] Nora: Redwood SEs help with model onboarding as part of the POC; we can assist with conversion and recommend quant profiles; for sensitive models we can do onboarding in your Private environment

[09:44] Tom: ok, what about rate limits? we might have bursts from background jobs, and we want graceful throttling not hard fails

[09:54] Liam: we support burst capacity and configurable rate limiting with retry/backoff behavior. For Dedicated you can configure burst pools and fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant if capacity is constrained

[10:10] Dr. Elena: any objections typically from teams like ours? what should we watch out for?

[10:18] Maya: procurement/ legal usually want to confirm data residency, SOC2, and indemnities; engineering focuses on tail latency and integration complexity; recommend getting the security questionnaire early so we can iterate quickly

[10:32] Samir: ok, on telemetry — we can provide synthetic workload and a small sample of de-identified logs by tomorrow, would that be enough to start sizing?

[10:42] Nora: yes that's perfect. we'll use that to run bench tests and propose a Dedicated pool size. we'll also capture P95/P99 numbers and cost per 1k tokens in the spreadsheet

[10:56] Alicia: one more on encryption in flight — do you support mTLS between services?

[11:04] Carlos: yes mTLS supported for Private and Dedicated data-plane connections; we'll include config snippets in the SSO/security doc

[11:20] Dr. Elena: ok let's talk pilot scope and timeline — you mentioned 2-4 weeks for pilot; we want a minimal set of features: ingest pipeline -> Redwood inference -> redact/logging -> summarization into EMR; is that practical?

[11:38] Liam: yes that's a typical flow. Redwood can be the inference layer; for redaction/PHI we recommend doing that upstream but we can help validate redaction in the flow

[11:50] Samir: do you folks offer prebuilt connectors to common EMRs?

[11:56] Maya: we don't ship full EMR connectors, but we have examples and plugins; usually customers build a thin adaptor; we can share sample code from other healthcare pilots (sanitized)

[12:10] Dr. Elena: wanted to flag governance — we will need to run a small eval on hallucination rates for clinical prompts, do you have eval tooling?

[12:20] Nora: yes Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; SEs can help set baselines and run evals during pilot

[12:36] Tom: will the Console surface per-prompt quality metrics?

[12:44] Liam: yes you can tag routes and prompt templates, and Optimize will surface regressions and alert on sample-level metrics

[12:58] Maya: ok wrapping up the technical part — we'll need three things from you to start: 1) sanitized telemetry / sample payloads, 2) procurement contact for SOW and PO, 3) security contact to complete questionnaire

[13:12] Dr. Elena: I can be procurement contact initially; Alicia will take security; Samir will send the infra details and samples

[13:22] Maya: perfect. action items we'll capture and send meeting notes after this call. anything else from the team?

[13:32] Samir: one small question about cost monitoring — can we get alerts if spend rises above threshold?

[13:40] Liam: yes billing alerts and per-route budget thresholds are supported, we can configure chargeback and notify via Slack or email

[13:52] Alicia: legal will also want to schedule a call with your security team; can we do that next week?

[13:58] Maya: yes we'll propose times, Nora and Carlos can join for deeper technical security Q&A

[14:08] Dr. Elena: ok thanks everyone, excited to get started

Recap (end of meeting):
- Pilot scope: Dedicated proof-of-concept for summarization flow; aim to validate P95 latency < 800ms, cost targets, and security posture
- Deliverables: Redwood to send onboarding checklist, SSO/SCIM quickstart, SOC2/DPA, Dedicated pricing and SOW, and SE-run benchmark plan
- Owners: Maya (send docs), Liam (coordinate pilot and SE deep dive), Samir (provide infra and sample payloads), Alicia (security questionnaire)
- Next meeting: SE deep dive to be scheduled by 2026-01-15

Links referenced: onboarding checklist (link in follow-up), SSO quickstart (link), pricing examples (link), benchmark spreadsheet (to be created by Redwood SE)

End of transcript.
